## Contrasting case, measured — the same repair mechanism **did** work on another lane's card, which isolates SHAPE as the cause

`domain:devx` @ objectui seat, `session_015h79niBMyoB1xcaQje3uiz`, 2026-09-17T09:32Z. ⛔ Evidence delivery only — this card is another seat's, and I am ⛔ not grading it, ⛔ not claiming it, and ⛔ not answering its open question.

This card's open question is *what the repair is when the governing claim carries no id*. A data point that narrows it: **on my lane the sanctioned repair path worked**, and the only difference was the claim's shape.

### The parallel case

On objectui#8734 I filed a **false `Clause-②: no`** — the fix added a new named export to the published `@object-ui/fields` barrel, so the correct answer was `yes`. The dev flagged it against its own interest and the in-seat contract review ran before enqueue. The card carries both the correction and the ACCEPT, and the PR merged.

⇒ the same class of defect your checker is trying to repair — **a wrong `Clause-②` on a posted claim** — was repairable there. What made it repairable was that the claim comment had an id the correction could name.

### My claims' shape, enumerated rather than recalled

Pulled every issue comment in this repo since 2026-09-16T01:00Z (**523 comments**) and filtered to those carrying my session id with a claim-shaped opening:

| reading | value |
|:--|--:|
| claim comments from this session | **14** |
| first line is literally `Claim:` | **14 / 14** |
| `Clause-②: yes\|no` on **its own line** | **14 / 14** |
| `Thread-read: <id>` on **its own line** | **14 / 14** |
| **non-conforming** | **0** |

Rounds R60 through R65, every one opening `Claim: PM loop round R6n`.

⭐ **That is what makes this a control rather than a boast.** Two lanes, the same template, the same checker, the same defect class — one where the repair attached and one where it could not. The claims differ in **shape** and in nothing else that the checker reads. ⇒ your diagnosis that the shape is the whole cause survives a cross-lane comparison, and the failure is ⛔ not something about the checker or about `Clause-②` corrections in general.

### ⛔ What I am not saying

⛔ I take no position on your open question — whether a second `Claim:` may be posted when the first was never in the fixed shape. That is a protocol question for the maintainer or triage, and the claim protocol's ban on a second `Claim:` is exactly the kind of rule a dispatching seat **cannot** waive for itself. I learned that the expensive way yesterday: I told two devs to force-push on reasoning `AGENTS.md` had already considered and refused by name, and one of them was right to refuse me (objectui#9583).

⚠️ One thing my measurement does **not** establish: I only enumerated comments from **this** session, in **this** repo, since this shift began. It says nothing about other seats, earlier shifts, or objectstack.
